result.builder:
Make one pull request that adds a --shout flag to the greet CLI and meets every line of the issue's expect list:
1. node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
2. without --shout the output is unchanged
3. docs/index.md documents --shout
4. after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Steps:
- Read bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml.
- In bin/greet.js, detect `--shout` in process.argv. The name is still the first argument that does not start with `--`, so `--shout` may come before or after the name. When `--shout` is present, print the greeting from src/greet.js in upper case (for example `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline). When it is absent, keep the current output exactly as it is (`Hello, Ada!` plus newline) and keep the usage error and exit code 2 when no name is given.
- Do not change the existing greeting() output in src/greet.js. If you add a helper there, export it separately.
- Add tests to test/greet.test.js: `--shout Ada` gives `HELLO, ADA!\n`, `Ada --shout` gives the same, and plain `Ada` still gives `Hello, Ada!\n`. Keep the existing tests passing. Run `npm test` and confirm it passes.
- Update docs/index.md to document `--shout`: show `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and say it prints the greeting in upper case (e.g. `HELLO, <NAME>!`). Keep the existing usage text.
- The published page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ is built by .github/workflows/pages.yml, which uploads the docs/ directory on pushes to main. Do not change that workflow. Updating docs/index.md is what makes the live page list --shout after merge; you cannot check the live page from the PR.
- Open the pull request and link https://github.com/o/greet-cli/issues/12 in its description.
result.verifier:
Run every check at the pull request's head. Run `npm install` first if it is needed (there are no dependencies). There is one check per expect line, in the issue's order.

Check 1. Expect line: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case".
Run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js Ada` from the repository root.
PASS: the output of the --shout run is the greeting from the plain run converted to upper case (expected `HELLO, ADA!`).
FAIL: the command errors, or its output is not the upper-case form of the greeting (for example it is unchanged, only partly upper case, or missing the name).

Check 2. Expect line: "without --shout the output is unchanged".
Run `node bin/greet.js Ada` at the PR head. Also run it on the PR's base commit (for example `git show <base>:bin/greet.js` and `git show <base>:src/greet.js` into a temporary directory, or a separate checkout of the base) and compare.
PASS: the output at the head without --shout is the same as at the base (`Hello, Ada!`).
FAIL: the output without --shout differs from the base output.

Check 3. Expect line: "docs/index.md documents --shout".
Read docs/index.md at the head.
PASS: the file mentions `--shout` and says what it does (upper-case / louder greeting).
FAIL: docs/index.md does not mention --shout, or mentions it without saying what it does.

Check 4. Expect line: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout".
The live page can only be seen after merge, so do not fetch it. Instead read what the head contains that will produce it: read .github/workflows/pages.yml and docs/index.md at the head.
PASS: the pages workflow still publishes the docs/ directory (the published page comes from docs/index.md) on pushes to the default branch, and docs/index.md at the head lists --shout. State in your report that the live page itself can only be seen after merge.
FAIL: the workflow no longer publishes docs/ (removed, path changed, trigger removed), or docs/index.md at the head does not list --shout.

Advisory (not pass/fail conditions):
- Run `npm test` and report whether it passes; check whether tests cover --shout.
- Try `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` (flag after the name) and report the output.
- Check that `node bin/greet.js` with no name still prints the usage message and exits with status 2.
- Exact expected strings: `HELLO, ADA!\n` with --shout, `Hello, Ada!\n` without.
